No, I don't think anyone can hear what I'm thinking. That would be pretty weird, wouldn't it? Like if my thoughts were just broadcasting out loud. The antenna was bent at this really sharp angle, almost like a lightning bolt. The pharmacy by my apartment just remodeled, actually, and they moved the entire beauty section to the back corner near the greeting cards. It's so confusing now, I couldn't even find the toothpaste last time I went in. I had to ask this clerk who looked like he was about twelve years old, and he just pointed vaguely toward the middle of the store. I don't feel like singing with my choir anymore, or having the softball team over to my place. I used to love hosting the softball team. We had this one game last summer where it started pouring rain right in the middle of the third inning. We all got completely soaked, and the mud out by second base was so thick my cleat actually got stuck in it. I had to hop back to the dugout with only one shoe on. It reminded me of that roller skate someone left at the depot, just sitting there all by itself. Anyway, we ordered pizza after that game from this place downtown that makes these huge, foldable slices. The crust was perfectly crispy, but the cheese slid right off when you picked it up. You had to do this weird head-tilt thing just to eat it without making a mess. I spilled tomato sauce all over my white jersey, and no matter how much bleach I used, there was always this faint orange stain right near the collar. I tried using this eco-friendly stain remover I found online, but it smelled strongly of pine needles, almost like a car air freshener. I hate those pine tree air fresheners, they always give me a headache. My dad used to hang one in his old pickup truck, and the smell would just bake into the upholstery during the summer. So, yeah, most days after my shift now, I just sit at the kitchen table with my planner open. I just stare at it, but I can't make myself start dinner, or make any calls, or do anything else, really.\n\nDoctor: Have you felt that thoughts were being put into your mind by someone or something else?\n\nPatient: Put into my mind? Thrift stores are great, but sometimes the clothes have that weird dusty smell, like old books. I love the smell of old books, though. There's this used bookstore downtown that has a whole basement full of first editions, and it smells exactly like vanilla and dust. The stairs going down there are super steep and creaky, and the wood is all worn down in the middle from people walking on them for years. The mop bucket was bright yellow, kind of like that raincoat I saw on the news.
